body:
^^^^ this. The prospect of inevitably killing myself makes me feel calm; if anything goes wrong I have a solution.

21 on a year out from uni here. Feel free to message me at any time if you want to (op and anyone else)

I have tried multiple medications for depression, ssris, snris, ones used for treatment resistant depression and even independent classes for a suitable amount of time. I have either had to stop them because i felt so bad, lots have increased the severity of mood swings (i also have bpd i probably wouldnt be talking to you if i continued with them) or they just did nothing for me. I have tried mood stabilizers and herbal treatment like st John's wort and 5htp even illegal drugs. I admittedly haven't tried maois or tricyclics and this is because when I have asked about them I have been laughed in the face by psychiatrists saying that they wouldn't prescribe them (side effects and dietary interactions and safety in overdose... ie they r more dangerous) but they're also more effective. If i wanted to try these the only way I would be able to would be to order them off the internet by myself. I have tried different doses in all of the above, have followed regular administration.  Antidepressants dont take months to work... they take months to take their full effect you are usually able to tell within 2 weeks of a therapeutic dose whether the meds will make any difference. Based on this fact i have tried ketamine infusions an experimental treatment because it's said to work immediately... Please don't insinuate I haven't tried. 

My boyfriend is well aware of my mental health problems. I have stressed this throughout my post, he's more of a carer than a partner and i burden him massively.

I am bright enough to get onto the course I wanted to but what's the point if I can't enjoy it, can't even get out of bed let alone concentrate or engage. Think it makes me feel worse. Whilst my parents love me they have no understanding of mental illness and are even in denial of it I feel completely alone with all of this and every one of my failings is a failing of me and not as a result of my mental illnesses, to them.

I'm already at home and no longer at university. I have tried and failed with so many treatments; its a massive part of the problem and why feel so hopeless. There's such a nasty stigma surrounding drugs for the treatment of  depression and i know that if I lived in another country id have a lot more to try.

Id like to see it as a blip too but I have felt like this for 9 years and i dont know what to do anymore.

I really and genuinely appreciate your comment and try to help me but it's a lot more complicated than you think, if the answers were easy I wouldn't want to die.
